description: tidycensus is Kyle Walker and contributors' R interface to United States Census Bureau tables and geographic boundaries. It requests decennial Census and American Community Survey data and returns tidyverse-ready data frames, optionally with simple-feature geometry. Inputs are requested variables, geography and survey settings; outputs are attribute tables or spatial data frames for analysis. Coverage is the United States, with years and geographic detail determined by each Census product. Source is free under MIT, confirmed in DESCRIPTION and the licence file. A limitation is that the README requires a free Census API key and the package is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau. Survey uncertainty and changing boundaries still need interpretation. The tool can prepare population and demand inputs for infrastructure simulations. Census commuting flows (data-us-census-acs-commuting-flows) are related data. Only public software documentation was inspected; no key or Census data was requested.
